aye. rest. hot water bottle and whatever is on telly at 2pm on a saturday. living the dream. cheers for the help with the wording.
just came in from a calving that took three hours. heifer, first calf, breech presentation with one leg back. absolute nightmare. calf is alive though so thats something.

shes up and nursing which is more than i expected honestly. gave her metacam and some calcium. shell be sore tomorrow but shell be fine. the farmer was panicking the whole time which didnt help. kept asking if we should just call it and do a section.

the leg was the issue. calf was big, heifer was tight, and the leg was folded right back under the body. couldnt get enough room to cup the hoof and bring it forward without risking tearing her. ended up having to repel the calf, get some lubricant in, and work the leg round slowly. took about 45 minutes just on that part.

the farmer was helping but hes about 70 and not the strongest. his grandson was there too, maybe 16, never seen a calving before. so i had the old man on the rope and the boy looking like he was about to pass out. crack team.

ropes on both hind legs once they were corrected, then steady traction. she was pushing well by that point which helped. the calf came out flat, not breathing, had to clear the airway and rub it down. took about a minute to start breathing which felt like about a year.

bit of cold water behind the ears aye. and vigorous rubbing with a towel. worked a treat. you know its funny, i did five years at edinburgh for the bvetmed and the thing that saved that calf was basically the same technique my dad showed me when i was about 12. rub them hard with straw til they cough.

aye fair point. i do use the anatomy more than i let on. knowing exactly where that leg is and how to manipulate it without doing damage, thats not something you learn from watching your dad. the first year farm placements at edinburgh were the most useful bit though. more than any lecture.

ill pop back tomorrow. want to check shes not got a retained placenta and make sure the calf is feeding properly. the farmer is experienced but he was pretty shaken tonight so id rather see it myself. plus the grandson will prob want to know if the calf has a name yet.
aye. im covered in amniotic fluid and i cant feel my right arm but the calf is alive so ill take it. right, need a shower and about 12 hours sleep. cheers.
well that was a morning. spent forty minutes trying to get the defender started in minus three. just sat there turning the key like a fool while a farmer watched from his kitchen window.

prob the glow plugs again. its a 98 so everything on it is original or held together with cable ties. more rust than actual metal at this point. farmer came out eventually and asked if I wanted a tow. very dignified.

it caught on the maybe fifteenth try. made a noise like a dying animal which is ironic given my line of work. then I had to drive it another twenty miles to the next farm with the heater not working. couldnt feel my hands by the time I got there.

aye its been at that point for about four years tbh. the thing is nothing else gets through the tracks I have to drive. half the farms up here dont have proper roads. just mud and rocks and the odd river crossing. the defender handles all of it. when it starts.

I phone the farmer and tell them ill be late. thats the backup plan. or if its really bad I borrow my neighbours wee suzuki jimny but trying to fit vet equipment in a jimny is like playing tetris with syringes.

once a month maybe. more in winter. the cold just kills it. and theres a leak somewhere that means the footwell fills up with water when it rains which up here is basically always. I keep wellies in the cab just to drive it.

wouldnt say emotionally attached. more like I know exactly how broken it is and a new vehicle would just be a different set of problems I havent learned yet. better the devil you know. also defenders hold their value weirdly well so selling it is always in the back of my mind but then id have to actually commit to something else.
aye. stuck is the right word. it got me home today so it lives another week. if it doesnt start tomorrow though its getting pushed into a ditch.
right. need to figure out my saturday. got a match at two and a farm call that was meant to be in the morning but the farmer just texted saying he cant do before noon. classic.

just a routine check on some ewes pre-lambing. shouldnt be more than an hour if nothing weird turns up. but weird always turns up. and then I need to get across to the rugby ground and changed by quarter to two which is pushing it.
nah the farmer is away sunday. ill just have to be efficient. wouldnt be the first time ive turned up to rugby smelling slightly of sheep. the lads are used to it.

winger. play for inverness highland rfc. been there about four years now. ngl im not fast enough for it anymore but nobody else wants the position so here we are. I just try not to get injured and call it a success.
league. caledonia division 2. were mid table which is about right for us. not good enough to go up not bad enough to go down. comfortable mediocrity. suits me fine tbh.
gordonians. theyre alright. big pack but their backs are nothing special. if our forwards can hold the scrum we should be fine. the problem is our forwards cant always hold the scrum.

aye its a bog. proper heavy. which doesnt help my speed situation. hard to sprint through six inches of mud when youre already the slowest winger in the division. at least it slows everyone else down too.
thats the dream. slightly of livestock rather than strongly of livestock. cheers.
got offered a job today. practice down in glasgow. decent money too. told them no before I even finished reading the email.
mixed practice but mostly small animal. dogs and cats. which is fine work but its not what I do. and its in glasgow which is the bigger problem.
the city itself. all of it. couldnt do it. not a chance. I need the hills and the quiet. glasgow would finish me off in about a week. the noise and the traffic and the people everywhere. no thanks.

aye. cant see any reason to leave. ive got the work I want right here. the hills are right there. I can drive ten minutes and not see another person for hours. why would I give that up to look at labradoodles in a consulting room.
fiona texted me five minutes after I told her. said I should take it so she could see me more. I said she could always move back up here. she said absolutely not. so we are at an impasse as usual.

prob about ten grand more. which is not nothing tbh. but ten grand doesnt buy you a view of ben wyvis from your kitchen window does it. and I dont have expensive tastes. I eat stew and drive a car thats older than some of my patients.
aye well. I know what I like and what I dont like. cities are firmly in the dont like column. always have been. ill stay up here till they carry me out.
just looked at my march diary. want to cry. not really but close.
tb testing. starts march. booked solid the first two weeks already and theyre still adding farms. two hundred cattle minimum by my count and thats conservative.

aye. inject them day one then go back 72 hours later to read the results. so every farm is two visits. and the cattle dont enjoy it and they make sure you know about it. my arm will be dead by the end of day one.

theres two of us on the rural team so we split it but its still a mountain. and the scheduling is a nightmare because you have to time the reads exactly. cant be early cant be late. so if anything overruns on day one the whole week goes sideways.

massive area aye. some of the farms are an hour apart. so half my day is driving and the other half is getting kicked by cattle. then you do the paperwork at night. DEFRA want every animal logged individually. its thrilling stuff.

both. I know exactly how bad its going to be which somehow makes it worse. like at least the first year I was naive about it. now I can feel the bruises in advance. my forearm gets properly swollen from doing the injections all day. the gun they give you for it is not exactly ergonomic.

ibuprofen and complaining mostly. ice it at night. swap hands when it gets really bad but im useless with my left so that just makes everything take longer. its fine. two weeks and its done. then its straight into lambing season so at least the pain changes location.
it will rain. it always rains. doing tb tests in the rain in a crush thats ankle deep in muck is the peak highland vet experience tbh. wouldnt swap it though. well. maybe for two weeks I would.
three breech lambs in one night. three. what are the odds of that.
two on the same farm and then got a call at half one in the morning for a third at a different place twenty miles up the road. hadnt even got my boots off from the first two.

first one was straightforward enough. got the legs sorted and pulled it out. good sized single lamb. alive and well. second one was trickier. twins and the first was breech. had to repel it and get the second one out first then go back for the breech. messy but both lived.

the third was the worst. ewe had been at it for hours before they called me. farmer tried to sort it himself first which I understand but by the time I got there the lamb was stuck and the ewe was exhausted. proper mess.

aye got it out eventually. had to use ropes. lamb was alive but weak. gave it some colostrum by tube and left the farmer with instructions to keep it warm and feed it every couple of hours. phoned him this morning and its doing alright. standing up at least.
sore but fine. gave her some pain relief and she was back on her feet within the hour. ewes are tough. more resilient than most of my human friends tbh. she just got on with it.

had about two hours sleep. been going on coffee since. hands are still covered in iodine that wont come off. got a wee bit of blood on my jacket that I only noticed when I stopped for petrol and the cashier looked at me like id committed a crime.
another three weeks at least. maybe four. it comes in waves. some nights nothing. some nights three breeches. no way to predict it. just have to keep the phone charged and the boots by the door.

aye well. the sheep dont send thank you cards but at least they dont send complaints either. right im going to try and get a nap before the phone goes again. if it goes again tonight I might just lie face down in the mud and stay there.
right so I've been looking into something and I want to think it through a bit before I commit to anything.

theres an equine surgery certificate I've had my eye on. been seeing more horse work come through the practice lately and theres proper demand for it up here. not many vets in the highlands that do equine surgery.

its a six month course. run through edinburgh. some of it is distance learning and some is practical blocks where you'd go down for a week at a time. so I could prob keep working through most of it but the practical weeks would mean I'm out of action for farm calls.

think its four practical blocks of a week each spread across the six months. coverage shouldnt be a huge issue. we've got locums we can bring in and tbh the other vets can absorb a week here and there. its more the cost thats giving me pause.

somewhere around eight grand all in. plus travel and accommodation for the edinburgh blocks. so prob closer to ten when you factor everything. employer might chip in a bit but I wouldnt bank on it being more than a token gesture tbh.

aye thats the thing. equine work pays well. way better than cattle and sheep per call. and theres estates up here with proper money that would rather have someone local than trailer a horse to glasgow or edinburgh. so the money side could work out fine in theory.

honestly I think its just the cost and the fact that I've never really done much horse work. cattle and sheep is what I know. horses are a different beast entirely. literally. but aye the demand is there and it would be good money so prob worth at least applying and seeing what happens.

think its september. so I've got time to think about it. might look into whether theres any bursaries or professional development funds I can tap into because ten grand out of pocket is a lot. but aye. worth exploring. cheers for helping me think it through.
the A9 is flooded again. third time this month. I had four farm calls booked this morning and Ive done precisely zero of them.

fully closed between beauly and muir of ord. police turning folk back. and the B roads arent much better because all the wee burns have burst their banks. tried the back road past kilmorack and there was about a foot of standing water across it. turned round.

one is a routine check. that can wait. two are hoof trims which arent urgent. the fourth is a ewe thats not eating and the farmer sounded worried on the phone. thats the one I need to get to but his farm is the other side of beauly which is exactly where the flooding is worst.

aye I've already asked him to send a video. hes about seventy and his phone skills are not what youd call advanced but he said his grandson would help. the thing is if its something like a blockage or a twisted stomach then a video isnt going to tell me much. needs hands on.

nearest other vet with large animal experience is prob dingwall and they'd have the same road problems coming from that direction. I could try going round by drumnadrochit and coming up the other side but thats adding an hour minimum and half those roads will be just as bad. honestly the highlands in april is just this. every year. you'd think the council would sort the drainage but no.

met office says heavy rain until early afternoon then easing. which in highland terms means it might stop by four or it might not stop until thursday. their forecasts are about as reliable as a chocolate teapot up here.

aye thats prob the plan. told him to keep her in the shed away from the others and keep an eye on her belly. if shes bloating he needs to call me straight away and ill find a way through regardless. just annoying. I should be working and instead im sat here watching the rain come down sideways.

dark chocolate and peat. aye that sounds right up my street. whats your take on the speyside peated ones. theres a few distilleries doing peated expressions now. benriach has one I think.

aye shes buzzing. phoned me at half seven this morning to tell me which is very fiona. no concept of the fact that some of us have been up since five dealing with a calving and might want five minutes peace. but aye shes over the moon.

aye about that. shes been a bit sick apparently but she says thats normal. shes a midwife so she knows the drill better than most. prob the best qualified person to be pregnant tbh. she already knows exactly whats happening at every stage.

thats very much the plan aye. show up. be entertaining for twenty minutes. hand it back the second anything comes out of either end. classic uncle protocol.

not yet. fiona has already sent me a list of things she doesnt want people to buy which is very her. no gendered stuff no plastic tat no noisy toys. I was going to get one of those wee highland cow soft toys because every scottish baby needs one and it'll wind fiona up which is a bonus.

wee tiny wellies. aye thats good. fiona will hate that. ill do both. right. suppose I should prob call her back and say something nice. I mostly just said oh right and aye cool when she told me which she was not impressed by.
aye. ill call her at lunch. maybe even say something borderline emotional. dont tell anyone.
I have spent the entire morning doing paperwork and I think I might actually lose my mind.

DEFRA stuff. cattle movement records. tb test documentation. herd health reports. every single thing has to be logged and filed and cross referenced with three other forms. I did not become a vet to be an administrator.

theres a new reporting requirement for bovine viral diarrhoea. BVD. came in this year. so on top of everything else theres now a whole separate set of forms for BVD screening results. and the online portal they want you to use barely functions. keeps timing out. had to re-enter the same data three times this morning.

scotland has had BVD eradication rules for a while through scotgov but now DEFRA is aligning the english and scottish systems which means more paperwork for everyone and a new portal that was clearly built by someone who has never met a cow. the interface is baffling. theres a dropdown menu for breed type and it doesnt include highland cattle. highland cattle. in scotland.

aye. other. every single time. and then theres a free text field where you type the breed and I guarantee nobody ever reads it. the whole thing is box ticking. nobody at DEFRA is sitting there going oh interesting another highland cow in the highlands. its just data going into a void.

honestly prob a full day a week. sometimes more. used to be half a day and that was annoying enough. its creeping up every year. new requirement here. new form there. and every time they say itll just take a few minutes. a few minutes multiplied by two hundred farms is not a few minutes.

theres software that does some of it but it doesnt talk to the new DEFRA portal properly. the formats dont match. so you end up exporting from one system and manually re-entering into the other which defeats the entire purpose. I looked into it last month. the integration is supposed to be coming but theyve been saying that for two years.

the BVA puts out statements about it every so often. reducing administrative burden on rural vets and all that. very strongly worded letters. nothing changes. the farmers complain about their end of it too. half of them cant use the portal either and end up phoning me to do it for them which is absolutely not my job but what are you going to do. theyre seventy years old and theyve been farming since before computers existed.

thats exactly it. designed from the top down by people who have never set foot on a farm. anyway. rant over. I need to go back and finish the forms before the portal times out again. cheers for listening.
right so I need a stew recipe that isnt going to be a total disaster. something I can make on sunday and eat for like 4 days. whats the best approach.
beef is fine. I can get it cheap from one of the farms so thats not an issue. the issue is ive made stew before and the meat ends up like shoe leather. every time. what am I doing wrong.
aye thats prob it then. ive been doing it on the hob on like medium heat for an hour and a half and calling it done. no wonder its terrible.
dont have a slow cooker. might get one tbh they seem like the kind of thing thats made for people who cant be bothered cooking properly. which is me.
aye alright ill look into it. what about veg. I usually just do carrots and tatties but its a bit boring after 4 days of the same thing.
dumplings. never made them. are they difficult.
right thats actually doable. even for me. the suet thing in a box — is that atora or whatever its called.
sound. right ill give this a go on sunday. stew in the oven for 3 hours, dumplings on top at the end. if it goes wrong im blaming you.
you know what. remember I was looking at doing extra qualifications. equine surgery cert. forget I said anything. its dead.

both tbh. looked at what the course actually costs and its absolutely mental. were talking thousands for a six month programme and thats before you factor in travel and materials and all the rest of it.

prob would have paid for itself eventually with the horse work up here but ngl I had a bit of a moment of honesty with myself. I dont even really like horses. massive dramatic creatures. everything is a crisis with them. one wee scratch and theyre acting like theyve been shot.

exactly. cattle are straightforward. they either have a problem or they dont. theres no performance about it. a cow doesnt make eye contact with you and tremble because theres a puddle. horses are just enormous toddlers with hooves.
zero. not even a wee bit. ill stick with cattle and sheep. they dont need me to like them and I dont need to pretend I enjoy being around them. its a professional relationship. works grand.

aye exactly. sometimes the smartest thing you can do is just not bother. the whole idea was a bad one from the start I think. got a bit carried away by the money side of it and forgot that id actually have to spend time with horses.
aye that would have been worse. much worse. sitting in a lecture about equine anatomy thinking what am I doing here. nah. its off the table completely. moving on.
they are not. theres always more cattle. theres always more sheep. job security through sheer volume of livestock. cant argue with that.
tell me honestly. have you ever watched a football team so consistently terrible that you start to think theyre doing it on purpose.
inverness caley thistle. been following them for years and every season I think surely this is the year they turn it around and every season they find new and creative ways to be absolutely dire.

aye. proper danger. not the kind where youre technically in the zone but prob fine. the kind where you look at the table and think right thats us then. the performances have been shocking. no goals. no ideas. just vibes and defeat.

bit of everything tbh. squad is thin. half the players look like they dont want to be there. the budget is nothing compared to teams around them. and the manager is doing his best with what hes got but you cant polish that level of performance.

making do. always making do. theyre not bringing anyone in that changes things. maybe a loan from a premiership reserve squad. some 19 year old who doesnt know where inverness is. thats the calibre were working with.

theyd survive but it would be grim. the attendances are already poor and if they drop down itll get worse. harder to attract players. harder to keep anyone decent. its a spiral. once you start going down its very hard to stop.

I still go when I can. not every week but enough. standing in the rain watching them lose 1-0 to a team from a town with 4000 people in it. thats the caley thistle experience. you dont go because its fun. you go because youve always gone.

theres a run of fixtures coming up against teams around them which could go either way. if they pick up a couple of wins theyve got a chance. if they lose those its pretty much done. but ive been saying that about must win games for about three months now and theyve won approximately none of them.
aye thats the one positive. I am impossible to disappoint at this point. theyve trained me. cheers for letting me vent about it. nobody else cares about caley thistle enough to listen.
quick question. when you start at a new practice do you reckon its better to bring your own equipment or just use whatever theyve got.
aye. just moved to a private practice. highland vets in inverness. left the nhs service a couple weeks back.

bit of both tbh. the money is better which obviously helps. but the equipment is miles ahead of what I was working with before. actually feels like a proper setup. and I dont have to drive to the middle of nowhere in caithness in the dead of winter anymore which is reason enough on its own.

similar. still mostly cattle and sheep. large animal. but the area is tighter. not covering half the highlands anymore. most farms are within 30-40 minutes which is luxury compared to what I was doing.
four vets including me. two vet nurses. small but its well run. everyone knows what theyre doing. less of the nhs bureaucracy as well which is nice. less paperwork more actual work.

one in four on call which is better than what it was. used to be basically on call all the time because there werent enough of us. now its one week on three weeks off. can actually plan my life a wee bit.

nothing major. still getting used to how they do things. every practice has its own way of doing stuff and you just have to adapt. some of the farmers dont know me yet so theres a bit of trust building to do. but thats normal.
aye exactly. one good calving and youre in. thats how it works. anyway cheers. ill prob just use their kit for now and see how it goes. no point bringing my own stuff if theirs is better.
got a farm with foot rot going through about 30% of the flock. 200 sheep. whats your take on the best treatment protocol for an outbreak at that scale.
aye its been boggy for weeks. classic conditions for it. they were in a low field near a burn and the drainage is terrible. farmer should have moved them earlier tbh but hindsight and all that.
no routine foot bathing. not unusual for the smaller farms up here. they just dont have the setup for it or the time. hes got a race but no proper foot bath.
hes on board now. took about 20 lame sheep to convince him but hes listening. hes asking about vaccination as well. is footvax worth it at this stage or is it too late for this outbreak.

aye ive used it before. the reactions can be nasty on some sheep. whats your view on culling the chronically affected ones. hes got maybe 5 or 6 that have been lame on and off for months. repeat offenders.

thats what I told him. he wasnt keen because some of them are good breeding ewes but I said youve got to look at it from a flock health perspective not an individual one. no point keeping a good ewe if shes making 10 others lame.

aye hes not got the fields for separation. its cull or nothing really. ill have another word with him about it. one more thing — how long before I should expect to see improvement in the ones were treating individually. like the paring and spray cases.
right thats helpful. ill schedule a recheck for next week then. cheers for the input. ill get the foot bathing set up this week and start working through the worst cases individually.
right so I need a decent waterproof for running in the hills. not a walking jacket. an actual running one. whats good these days.

daily training mostly. I run in the highlands so conditions are basically hostile sept through march. horizontal rain. 40mph wind on the ridges. needs to actually work not just look good on a mannequin in cotswold outdoor.
prob 150-200 quid. dont mind paying for something thatll last. the shakedry thing sounds interesting but if its fragile thats a problem. im not exactly gentle with my kit tbh.

aye thats a good point about the hem. my old running jacket was basically a wind funnel from the waist down. useless. whats the inov8 hood like. can you cinch it properly or is it one of those wee floppy things.
fiddly with cold wet hands. so every single time id use it then. brilliant. is the kamleika worth a look or is that more of a walking jacket.

own both. aye thats the dream. might start with the stormshell given where I am and what the weather does here. can always add the kamleika later for the nicer days. when its only raining sideways and not also trying to knock you off the hill.
cheers thats actually helpful. ill order the stormshell and see how it goes. if it keeps me dry on ben wyvis in october ill consider it a success.
so theres a planning application for a wind turbine near my village and the community meeting last night was absolute chaos. need to get my head around the actual facts here.

single turbine. commercial size though. 80 metres to tip. going on farmland about 800m from the nearest houses. the farmer wants it for the income which fair enough. but half the village thinks itll ruin the landscape and the other half thinks anyone who objects is a nimby. I honestly dont know where I stand.

open farmland but with hills behind. not exactly flat. theres already pylons along the road about a mile away so its not like the view is pristine as it is. the noise thing is what some folk were most upset about. one woman was saying theyd never be able to sleep again which seemed a bit dramatic.

there was some kind of assessment aye but nobody at the meeting had actually read it. myself included tbh. they were all just going off vibes. the farmer presented his case and then it descended into people shouting about eagles.

aye thats sensible. ill look it up. my gut feeling is that one turbine on farmland is probably fine and the landscape argument is weak when theres pylons already. but I work on farms round here and if theres a genuine eagle risk then thats different. seen golden eagles on that ridge a few times.

aye exactly. im not against it. wind energy is fine. just want the eagle thing looked at properly because if one gets killed by a turbine blade the whole village will lose its mind and theyll blame the folk who supported it. which would include me.
cheers. ill do that this weekend. better than just shouting at the next meeting anyway.
quick question. whats an appropriate gift for a 3 month old. asking for uncle purposes.

not very sentimental tbh. I already got her a thing when she was born. wee lamb toy. seemed on brand. now I just want to get something useful for when I visit next weekend. dont want to show up empty handed.

food for the parents is smart actually. my sister would prob appreciate that more than another outfit. shes been saying shes living off toast and coffee. which is what she was living off before the baby so not sure much has changed.

thats exactly the plan. ill believe its a real smile privately but ill tell her its gas. thats the arrangement. right cheers for the gift advice. stew it is. maybe a wee cake as well.
whats the best way to get mud off a hilux flatbed without scratching the liner. just got the thing and already treating it like its made of glass.
factory one. its the invincible spec so it came with the liner already in. prob overthinking it tbh. just not used to having a vehicle thats actually new. my last one was 27 years old.

aye its my work truck. im a vet so its full of kit. drugs cabinet bolted in the back. calving ropes. the usual. the old defender had all that too but everything in it was covered in a layer of mud and cow muck and I think at some point I just stopped caring. now ive got a clean truck and I want to keep it that way for at least a month.

gearbox went. again. third time. first two times I got it fixed but this time the mechanic basically said the whole drivetrain was done and it would cost more than the truck was worth to sort it. which tbh was probably true about five years ago as well I just kept ignoring that.

sold it to a lad who restores them. got more for it than I expected tbh. defenders hold their value even when theyre basically dead. he seemed genuinely excited about it which I found baffling but good luck to him.
the heater. aye. the defenders heater had two settings. off and slightly less cold. already had the hilux heater on this morning and it was actually warm within about 30 seconds. felt like cheating.

thats a fair point actually. used to sit in the defender for ten minutes before calls just to defrost my hands enough to examine an animal. the hilux I can just get out and get on with it. still feels wrong that nothing rattles though. too quiet. cheers for the cleaning tips anyway. ill enjoy the novelty while it lasts.
whats a reasonable target time for a first fell race. 10k distance. about 600m of ascent.
fairly new to running specifically. been fit though. played rugby for years but packed that in recently. my body was telling me it was time to stop getting tackled every weekend basically.

couple of months. been doing 3-4 runs a week since I stopped rugby. mostly routes around inverness. ben wyvis a couple of times. some of the wee hills closer to town for shorter runs. its a different kind of knackered to rugby. legs feel it more but I dont feel like ive been hit by a van on sunday morning which is an improvement.
the descending thing is where I feel most useless honestly. going up I can just grind. coming down I look like a baby deer on ice. everyone overtakes me on the downhills.

controlled falling. aye that makes sense. I think my problem is im basically braking the whole way down. every step. hammering my knees which is one of the reasons I stopped rugby in the first place so slightly counterproductive.

knees mostly. and I have crohns which doesnt mix great with contact sport. the flares were getting worse and the recovery time after matches was getting longer. felt like I was just making myself ill every weekend for a sport I wasnt even that good at anymore. fell running is better for me. its just the hills and my own legs. no one smashing into me. can stop when I need to.
stubbornness pointed uphill. aye thats about right. cheers for the training tips. ill work on the descending and just try to get round that first race in one piece.

absolutely rotten day. three call outs before lunch and the hilux is making a grinding noise that I do not want to think about. also forgot my lunch which means I ate a twix from a petrol station and called it nutrition.
think its the brakes aye. front left. going to get it looked at on saturday if I can be bothered. prob just pads. better than the last vehicle anyway, at least this one starts in the morning.

aye mental. had a cow with a displaced abomasum on tuesday, two foot trims yesterday, and today was just back to back routine stuff. practice has been flat out since october tbh. good problem to have I suppose.
right flank job. went fine though, farmer was happy. had eilidh assisting which makes things easier. she actually knows what shes doing unlike some folk ive worked with.
aye. shes been there about a year now. shes good. actually weve sort of been seeing each other for a wee bit. early days. not making a big thing of it.

aye its fine. shes sound. she gets it, like she doesnt bat an eye when I get called out at half ten on a sunday because some farmer thinks his sheep is dying. because she would prob get called out too. just works.

exactly. anyway its early days so im not going to sit here analysing it. just seeing how it goes. shes good company and she can drive a quad bike better than me which is mildly humiliating but mostly impressive.
aye. right I need to go sort out invoices before I lose the will entirely. cheers.
need a decent chilli recipe. im doing batch cooking on sunday so I can just reheat stuff through the week instead of eating cereal for dinner like some kind of feral student.
thats roughly what ive done before aye. couple of questions though. is it worth doing it in the slow cooker or is that just making life more complicated for the same result.

aye thatll work. I can brown the mince before I go for a run and let it do its thing while im out. other question. dark chocolate. ive seen folk put it in chilli. is that actually good or is it one of those things people say to sound interesting.

right ill give it a go. worst case its ruined and I go back to cereal. also thinking of doing rice portions separately in the freezer. just microwave a portion of each and thats dinner in five minutes.

jacket potatoes is a shout actually. might do half and half. right so the plan is. sunday morning run. come back. brown the mince. slow cooker on for the afternoon. rice and potatoes in the gaps. thats me sorted for the week.
low bar but aye. cheers for the recipe. ill report back on the chocolate situation.
bit stiff today. went up arthurs seat yesterday morning and my calves are not happy about it. forgot how steep the last bit is.
weekend aye. ive been down most weekends lately tbh. eilidh has a flat in stockbridge so ive just been staying there. its actually quite nice round that way.

aye more than I expected. theres a wee coffee place on raeburn place that does a flat white thats prob the best ive ever had. and stockbridge market on a sunday is decent. went last week and got some proper sourdough and a venison pie.
three and a bit aye. its fine though. leave friday after work, straight down the A9. put a podcast on and its not bad. and the roads are quiet that time of night.

nah not really. edinburgh is different from most cities tbh. you can see the hills from basically everywhere. and stockbridge doesnt feel properly urban. theres trees and the river and its walkable. its not like being dropped into glasgow city centre or something.
aye exactly. we did the botanics on saturday afternoon too which was grand. weirdly relaxing just wandering about looking at plants. never thought id say that but here we are.
aye it works. monday morning I go from flat whites and sourdough back to standing in a field with my arm inside a cow. keeps life interesting I suppose.
exactly. right I need to go stretch these calves out before they seize up completely. cheers.
thinking about doing ben macdui this weekend. as a run not a walk. been looking at the route from the ski centre car park at cairn gorm. is that the standard way up or is there a better option.
prob link both summits aye. if im going to be up there already seems daft not to. whats the terrain like on the plateau bit between the two. is it runnable or is it all boulders.

saturday is meant to be clear in the morning with cloud coming in from the west around midday. so the plan would be early start, up and back before it closes in. prob leave the car park by half seven.

aye ill take the micro spikes. theres definitely snow above about 900m right now. not planning on running through anything sketchy, if its icy on the steeper bits ill walk them. not worth a broken ankle.

aye full mountain kit. spare layer, waterproof, bivvy bag, headtorch, map and compass as well as the gps. emergency food. its the cairngorms in february not a park run. the wind chill up there can be minus twenty if it turns.

good shout. ill check SAIS on friday night. not planning on going near any steep convex slopes but good to know what the snowpack is doing. last time I was up in the cairngorms in winter there was proper spindrift across the plateau. couldnt see ten metres. turned back.
aye fingers crossed. would be nice to actually see the view from the top for once instead of just standing in a cloud wondering why I do this to myself. right cheers for the route chat.
got an email today that has properly dampened my mood. practice conference. two full days of powerpoints and networking. genuinely cannot think of anything worse.

may 8th and 9th. edinburgh. and aye its mandatory, the practice is paying for it so they expect everyone to go. two days of sitting in a conference centre listening to people talk about things I could read in a pdf in ten minutes.
think its one of those hotel conference places near haymarket. not sure exactly. the email was light on details and heavy on enthusiasm which is never a good sign.

mixture apparently. some clinical updates which might actually be useful. parasitology, antimicrobial stewardship, that kind of thing. but theres also a whole afternoon on practice management and client communication which is code for someone telling me to smile more at farmers.

prob drive down the 7th aye. practice is covering hotel rooms but I might just stay at eilidhs flat since shes in stockbridge anyway. save them the money and save me from making small talk at a hotel breakfast.
exactly. at least the evenings are mine. theres a couple of decent pubs on rose street. plan is to survive the powerpoints then go get a proper pint and pretend the next day isnt happening.
aye thats what I keep telling myself. at least its not three days. and edinburgh in may should be alright weather wise. could be worse, could be a conference centre in birmingham in november.
thats going on my gravestone. two days of moderate suffering with decent pints at the end. right I need to go. got a ewe with a prolapse waiting for me. more fun than a conference.
just spent three hours with my arm inside a cow and I am absolutely buzzing. well. buzzing for me which means slightly less tired than usual.
prolapsed uterus on a charolais cross. massive girl, prob 700kg. the whole thing was just hanging there when I turned up. farmer was white as a sheet, thought she was done for.

he reckoned maybe an hour. could have been worse tbh. the placenta was still attached which complicated things but at least it wasnt freezing so the tissue hadnt started to swell too badly. got her in the crush and cracked on.

aye sugar first to draw the oedema out. classic trick but it works. then it was just the usual wrestling match. trying to get 30kg of uterus back through an opening thats not exactly designed for the return journey. every time I got half of it in shed strain and the whole lot would come back out.

should have done one from the start honestly. I was being optimistic. gave her the caudal epidural after the third failed attempt and it was like a different cow. just stood there calmly while I worked it back in. then stitched a buhner suture to keep it in place.

aye he went from thinking he was losing a cow to offering me a bacon roll and a dram. which I accepted obviously. the cow was up and eating within twenty minutes which is always a good sign. shell be fine.
ill go back in about ten days to take it out. assuming she behaves herself. charolais are mental at the best of times so no guarantees she wont have done something equally dramatic by then.
aye me too. right I need a shower cos I smell like the inside of a cow. which is accurate. cheers.
settle something for me. speyside or islay. and dont give me a diplomatic both are great answer.
islay. no contest. if I wanted something smooth and inoffensive id drink ribena. whisky should taste like something actually happened to it.
laphroaig quarter cask most of the time. its like drinking a campfire next to the sea. perfect. ardbeg uigeadail if im feeling fancy which is almost never.

see thats the one speyside bottle I can respect actually. abunadh is decent. but most speyside stuff is just sherry and honey and nothing else. its whisky for people who dont really like whisky. balvenie doublewood is basically a dessert.

I work outside in the highlands in february. I dont want subtle. I want to come home, pour something that smells like a peat bog, and feel it in my chest. subtlety is for people with office jobs and underfloor heating.

highland park is alright. old pulteney is decent, quite like that one actually. its got a bit of salt to it cos its right on the coast in wick. but neither of them are islay. islay is just a different league for peat. the whole island smells of it when you step off the ferry.

aye went a couple years back. did laphroaig, ardbeg, and lagavulin in one day. which was a mistake in terms of remaining upright but a great day for the palate. lagavulin 16 straight from the distillery is something else. nearly wept. well. I thought about weeping. close enough for me.
aye got a distillery exclusive laphroaig that was finished in some kind of weird cask. cant remember what. it was good though. gone now obviously. didnt last the month.
aye. peat smoke or go home. speyside can be the backup for when the good stuff runs out. which it never does because I keep buying laphroaig. system works. right ta.
my sister is trying to pick a name for her wee one and I have been winding her up about it all week. its the most fun ive had in months.
told her she should call the bairn hamish. then when she said no I suggested angus. then fergus. then magnus. basically just going through every name that sounds like a highland cow.
she told me to stop texting her or shed block me. which she wont because she needs me to babysit. thats my leverage and she knows it.
normal ones. boring ones. she keeps going back and forth between about fifteen options and asking me what I think. and every time I just say hamish again. its a perfect system.
aye her partner has opinions but fiona is fiona. she will decide and he will agree. thats how it works in our family. the women decide things and the men nod.

ngl I actually quite like the name ruairidh which she had on the list at one point. but I made the mistake of saying that so now she says its ruined because she pictures me saying it. apparently I say everything in a tone that makes it sound sarcastic.

aye but then id lose momentum on the hamish campaign and I canny have that. sent her a wee picture of a highland cow today with the caption 'uncle callum took hamish for a walk'. she left me on read for four hours.

prob. honestly whatever she picks ill be happy. im just enjoying winding her up because thats what brothers are for. the bairn could be called anything and id still be there every weekend making faces at it.
terrible naming consultant is going on my cv right under farm veterinarian. right im off to think of more cow names. cheers.
one of the other vets just got an isuzu d-max and wont shut up about it. keeps telling me I should swap the hilux. need to know if hes actually right or if im justified in ignoring him.
says the payload is better, the towing capacity is better, and its cheaper. which I think is three arguments but hes counting it as one big argument. also says the ride is smoother.
its a 2025. not had a single issue with it. starts every morning, goes through anything, doesnt complain. which is more than I can say for most of my colleagues. human and animal.

aye its grand. not as good off road as my old vehicle was tbh but thats a high bar. the hilux handles the tracks fine, its just a bit wider so some of the tighter gates are a squeeze. but it gets through. and crucially the heater works which is a luxury I never had before.

prob worse actually. his looks massive. like a vehicle thats been to the gym. all the new pickups are just getting wider and taller for no reason. the farmers up here have gates from the 1940s. nobody is making them bigger to accommodate our midlife crisis trucks.

aye the bed is fine for kit. ive got a canopy on it so everything stays dry. got the drugs box bolted in, calving ropes, the scanner, all the usual stuff. it works. thats all I need from a vehicle. it works and it starts.
aye lets just say ive had vehicles where starting was more of a suggestion than a guarantee. those days are behind me. the hilux just turns on like a normal machine. revolutionary concept.

ill tell him his d-max is very nice and then continue driving my hilux until it dies. which based on toyota reliability will be roughly 2045. by which point ill be too old to care about trucks. perfect plan.
aye. right cheers for confirming what I already knew. just needed external validation. ta.
weird mood today. sat in the truck after my last call and just sort of thought about things for a bit. not in a bad way. just reflecting I suppose.

just how things have gone this past while. moving to private practice was a big decision and I spent ages going back and forth on it. but sitting there today after a good call on a nice farm I thought aye. this was right.

nothing dramatic. just a routine fertility check on some heifers. farmer was sound, weather was decent for once, cows behaved themselves. I was done by three and drove home with the window down. thats it. thats the whole thing. and it was enough.

aye much rarer. I was stretched so thin before. covering too much ground, always behind, always knackered. now the caseload is manageable and I actually have time to do the job properly. which sounds basic but it makes a massive difference when youre up to your elbows in a cow.

prob aye. not that it was bad before but when youre tired and rushed you cut corners without meaning to. now I can take my time, talk to the farmer properly, actually think about what im seeing instead of just reacting. the crohns is better managed too when im not running on four hours sleep.
